thought: His village had no electricity until he was seven. He now leads Australia's national academy of science.
support: Chennupati Jagadish grew up in the farming village of Vallurupalem, Andhra Pradesh, where his village had no electricity until he was about seven years old and he studied at night by kerosene lamp. He walked roughly 5 kilometers barefoot each day to reach school. He moved to Australia in 1990 with his wife and 2-month-old daughter, and became a Distinguished Professor at the Australian National University, leading its Semiconductor Optoelectronics and Nanotechnology Group. In 2022, he was elected President of the Australian Academy of Science - the first person of Indian origin to hold the role.
